summary: Ashok Kumar Chatterjee (1925–2021) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti, heading philosophy departments at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University (1950–1963) and BHU (1963–1985).
Ashok Kumar Malhotra (b. 1940) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the East-West Center. He founded the Yoga and Meditation Society for the Scientific Study of Spirituality.

Ashok Ramchandra Kelkar (1929–2014) specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Cornell University (~1956–1958). He held posts at Pune, Agra University (~1962–1967), and Deccan College (~1967–1989) as Professor of Applied Linguistics.

Ashoka Welitota is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Senior Lecturer Gr. II at the University of Kelaniya in 2016 and as Senior Lecturer at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Ashutosh Mishra earned an MLIS at the Central University of Gujarat (2020–2022). He held library posts at the Institute of Rural Management Anand (2022–2024), Bennett University (2024), and Parul University (2024–2026).

Ashutosh Mukherjee (1864–1924) studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta (BA 1883). He was Calcutta High Court judge (1904), Tagore Professor of Law (1906–1914), and President of The Asiatic Society (~1907–1915), later founding Asutosh College (1916).

Ashutosh Pareek is an Indologist who earned a PhD at Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Rajasthan Sanskrit University (2012). He has been a professor at Samrat Prithviraj Chauhan Government College since 2008 and visiting faculty at Hindu University of America.

Asim Kumar Chatterjee (b. 1940) specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Calcutta under D. Mukherjee in 1967, later serving as Senior Research Fellow there (attested 1970) and lecturer at Jangipur College.

Asko Parpola (b. 1941) is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto at the University of Helsinki (PhD 1968). He held posts at NIAS (1968), the Academy of Finland, and served as professor at Helsinki (~1982–2020).
Assa Doron is an Indologist who earned his PhD from La Trobe University (2000–2005). He was appointed Professor at the Australian National University in 2007.

Astley John Hilary Goodwin (1900–1959) was an archaeologist who studied at Selwyn College (1919–1922) and SOAS University of London (1922). He held a post at the University of Cape Town beginning in 1923.

Astrid Zotter is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Leipzig. She has held posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018) and Heidelberg University (attested 2023).
Athanaric Huard is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Georges-Jean Pinault and served as an assistant at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).
Athanasius Pryor Treweek (1911–1995) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Sydney (~1929–1934), where he became Professor of Greek in 1938.

Atsuhiko Yoshida (b. 1934) studied at Seikei, Tokyo, Strasbourg, and the EPHE under Georges Dumézil. Specializing in religious studies and history/archaeology, he worked at CNRS (~1960–1969) and was a professor at Seikei University (1970) and Gakushuin University (2006).

Atsuki Nakagami works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Nakagami held posts as a visiting researcher at the University of Hamburg (attested 2022) and at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
Atsushi Ibuki (b. 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1978–1988) and became a professor at Toyo University around 2005.

Atsushi Kanazawa (b. 1951) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1981), specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He lectured at Meteorological College (~1985–1991) and served as assistant professor and professor at Komazawa University (~1996–2017).

Atsushi Kiyozawa (b. 1951) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Delhi and held a lecturer position at Kindai University around 1989.

Atsushi Uno (b. 1922) studied at Kyoto and BHU under T. R. V. Murti, Raghunath Giri, and others. Specializing in Indology and philosophy, he was professor at Tokai (1971), Hiroshima (1974–1986), and Kindai University (~1986–1993).
